title: Interviewer Debias Scorecard and Compact Probe Kit
summary: Compact, actionable scorecard + probe bank for interviewers to reduce bias, calibrate signals, and speed debriefs. Built for distributed interview panels and mixed experience levels.
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact interviewer-facing tool: a de-bias checklist, a three-axis scorecard, sample probes (compact), and an async debrief template. Goal: make interviews faster, reduce common heuristics that leak bias, and anchor hiring decisions to observable behavior across role-level anchors.

Audience:
- interviewers (engineers, PMs, managers)
- hiring managers and panel leads
- people ops interview facilitators

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Panels are inconsistent: different interviewers weight signals differently.
- Halo/contrast effects and similarity bias creep into decisions.
- Remote panels have less shared context and shorter debrief windows.
- We need a repeatable, low-friction artifact to capture signals and reduce guesswork.

Quick instructions for interviewers (use this doc during interview):
1) Before the interview (10m): skim the role anchors below, pick 2–3 probes you own from the probe bank.
2) During interview: ask at least one behavioral + one technical/compositional probe. Stick to follow-ups in the rubric (SEE FOLLOW-UPS).
3) After interview (5–10m): fill scorecard, leave 1–2 succinct evidence bullets, tag anything that needs manager attention. Submit before leaving calendar block.

DE-BIAS CHECKLIST (pre & post)
- Pre: read candidate résumé quickly but do NOT form a hiring stance. Focus on role anchors.
- Pre: note potential identity signals (career break, non-traditional background) and commit to evidence-first scoring.
- During: avoid early verdicts; if you catch yourself thinking "fit" quickly, ask for one more anchor behavior.
- Post: when you write evidence, avoid adjectives (e.g., "smart"). Prefer: "wrote a short algorithm to X" or "described tradeoffs between A and B".
- Panel: use the numeric score, then discuss 1–2 concrete risks/uncertainties. 

THREE-AXIS SCORECARD (compact) — fill each as number + 1 short evidence bullet
1) Core competency (role-specific skills) — 1..5
   Anchor examples: for engineers: system design clarity, coding composure, debugging heuristics.
2) Problem solving & learning approach — 1..5
   Anchor examples: structured troubleshooting, ability to generalize, method for unknowns.
3) Collaboration & communication — 1..5
   Anchor examples: accepts feedback, explains tradeoffs to non-technical partners, asynchronous writing clarity.

Scoring guidance (quick):
- 5 = exceptional: multiple clear, replicable examples, independent at role level.
- 3 = solid mid: meets expectations with small coaching areas.
- 1 = insufficient: misses multiple anchors, requires strong dev.

OVERALL RECOMMENDATION (choose one): Strong hire | Hire with reservations (list key risk) | No hire | Hold for follow-up (specify follow-up)

EVIDENCE NOTES (2 bullets max):
- Evidence should be short actions/quotes or described steps (e.g., "wrote unit-test-driven patch under time; explained tradeoffs A vs B").

RISK TAGS (optional):
- domain-experience | leadership-ambition-mismatch | communication-limited | reliability-unknown | salary-expectation-mismatch

FOLLOW-UPS (if recommending hold or hire-with-reservations)
- ask hiring manager to run a short take-home focusing on the uncertain axis (3–4 hours).
- schedule a follow-up chat for clarifying timeline/compensation expectations.

COMPACT PROBE BANK (pick probes labeled B=behavioral, T=technical, C=comp)
- B1: Tell me about a time you shipped something that failed in production. What happened, what did you do, and what changed afterward? (Follow-up: how did you measure the rollback vs fix decision?)
- B2: Describe a time you changed your mind after receiving feedback. What was the feedback, and how did you adapt? (Look for specific observable steps.)
- T1: Given a streaming system that needs to maintain per-user KV state for 10M users with 100k TPS, sketch a high-level partitioning and failure-recovery strategy. (Follow-up: tradeoffs on consistency vs latency.)
- T2: Live coding (30m): refactor the helper to remove an O(n^2) path. Ask candidate to explain complexity before coding. (Follow-up: test cases they would add.)
- C1: System composition probe: Integrate an LLM-based inference pipeline with existing auth and rate limits. What are the key safety and cost controls you would add? (Look for telemetry & fallback ideas.)
- C2: Design-for-maintainability: You inherit a monolith with slow CI. Prioritize 3 changes in the first quarter and justify. (Follow-up: what are metrics to track?)

Probe picking notes:
- Aim for 2–3 probes total in each interview. Mix B+T/C where role needs both.
- For junior candidates prefer B + 1 simple T (smaller surface).
- For senior hires favor system composition + leadership probes.

EXAMPLE MINI-RUBRIC PROMPTS (how to follow-up to elicit evidence)
- "Walk me through exact steps you took — what code or data did you inspect?"
- "What did you try that didn't work?"
- "How did you involve others and what was the split of work?"

ASYNC DEBRIEF TEMPLATE (paste into calendar comment or hiring tool)
- Candidate: [name] | Role: [role] | Interviewer: [you]
- Scores: Core X/5 | Problem X/5 | Comm X/5
- Short evidence (2 bullets):
  - 
  - 
- Recommendation: [Strong hire / Hire with reservations / No hire / Hold for follow-up]
- Key risk(s) and suggested follow-up (if any):

CALIBRATION EXERCISE (run quarterly with panel leads)
- Pick 3 anonymized debriefs, have each interviewer re-score using anchors, then run 15m discussion. Document shifts and add to "anchor bank".

ONBOARDING HANDOFF CHECKLIST (if hire) — hand to hiring manager and onboarding partner
- 1-pager: candidate strengths & top 3 ramp tasks.
- Access needs: repos, CI, infra, slack channels — list urgent ones.
- First 30-day learning plan: pair rotations, code reading, small high-impact bug to own.

Open items / To iterate on (notes to self):
- Add role-specific anchor tables for SDE-I / SDE-II / Senior / Staff with sample signals.
- Collect 10 short quotes from hiring managers about what they value in evidence (to calibrate anchors).
- Integrate with hiring score export (People Ops tool) so tags map to downstream reports.

Risks and guardrails we want to enforce:
- No single interviewer should veto without evidence and 1 concrete example.
- Avoid higher weight for on-site charisma vs structured signals (code, decisions, outcomes).

Changelog (short):
- 2025-05-12 Ava R: created initial draft and probe bank.
- 2025-05-20 Maya C: added async debrief template and de-bias checklist bullets.
- 2025-06-02 Ethan P: updated probe guidance and onboarding handoff checklist.

Notes to interview coordinators:
- Encourage panels to leave 10m at end of loop for synchronous 5m alignment if possible.
- If interviewers are junior, pair them with a senior interviewer and require at least one shared question to anchor evaluation.

---
This is a working doc. Please add examples and real debrief snippets (anonymized) to the bottom so new interviewers can learn from concrete writing.
